find: One of Turnly’s most striking dramatic methods is the use of language as a marker of identity and coercion. In the North Korean scenes, English stands in for Japanese (the language Hanako speaks at home and later teaches) and stylised Korean signals that she is now living inside a system that wants to erase who she is. This code-switching is a form of subtext: every time Hanako speaks in the language she has been forced to learn, the audience feels the cost of her survival.

In several scenes, dialogue begins in Japanese or Korean before returning to English so the audience can follow it. This code-switching can make identity and power audible: Hanako teaches Japanese to Jung Sun while living under coercion in North Korea.
